log: WHAT IS AUC 0.617 MEASURING? -- decompose it against the parameter-free feature floor
GeoConv sees a ~6 A patch (K=16 neighbours) and 5 per-point features. Before calling 0.617 a
learned result, measure how much of it is available with NO model: raw features multiplied.
The task is largely 'are BOTH points interface points', since positives are contacts and
negatives are far pairs -- not a genuine test that two patches FIT.
PREDECLARED: a single raw feature near 0.60 => the network adds almost nothing and 0.617 is
local chemistry already present in the input. All arms at 0.50 => the aggregation earned it.
NO COORDINATES in any arm -- position would make the task trivial.
54 complexes | train 40 | eval 14 (identical split to dock_arch)
eval pairs: 795 contacting / 2,665 far
PARAMETER-FREE ARMS (one feature, one operation, nothing fitted)
feature              product   similarity
apbs_potential        0.4343       0.4736
curvature             0.4633       0.5591
hydrophobicity        0.4956       0.4739
(0.5 = chance; a value BELOW 0.5 is informative with the sign flipped)
best single feature, sign-corrected: apbs_potential at 0.5657
FITTED, NO GEOMETRY: logistic over 10 pair features (5 products + 5 abs-diffs) = 0.5467
GEOCONV (dock_arch, same split): 0.6171
network minus best single feature : +0.0514
network minus fitted logistic     : +0.0704
READING
THE AGGREGATION EARNS IT. Best single feature 0.5657, fitted logistic 0.5467, both
well under the network's 0.6171. The K=16 neighbourhood is contributing real
structure beyond what the per-point features contain.
Either way 0.617 is a WEAK number in absolute terms: on a task whose negatives are pairs >12 A
apart -- the easy negatives -- it ranks the contacting pair first barely 3 times in 5.
